subject: headcrab

measured.lineup: ours is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/chumtoad.mdl, models/roach.mdl, models/leech.mdl: the judge does not know which

M1.reason: The overall outline fits the brief's low, splayed, four-legged crawler with a mouth beneath (FRONT, LEFT, FRONT-LEFT). It is short of the brief in two places: the legs read as thin, stiff spikes (LEFT, RIGHT) rather than legs, and the sharp front claws are absent from the outline (FRONT, FRONT-LEFT, FRONT-RIGHT show no claw tips at the front).

M2.reason: Measured 25.5 long against the asked 26 (2% off) and 13 high against 13 (exact). Both are within 15%.

M3.reason: Listed parts: fleshy body (present, one dome), four clawed legs (present as four tapering spikes, but with no distinct claws on their ends, as FRONT-LEFT and BACK-RIGHT show), a beak-like mouth underneath (present, the yellow-green cone visible in BELOW and TOP at the front), and sharp front claws (absent as a separate part; the front legs are the same spikes as the rear ones). A missing small part caps M3 at 1.

M4.reason: The body is the tan the brief asks for, and the beak is a sensible yellow-green. But the surface is a matte, faceted, grainy texture that reads as wood, sand or cardboard (TOP, BELOW, FRONT), not fleshy skin. The brief's material is not conveyed on the body or legs.

M5.reason: The brief asks for no markings, lettering or panel lines. The faint radial grain on the dome and legs adds nothing wrong, so this is scored 2 as a plain surface.

M6.reason: In lineup.png the tan dome with four spikes and a yellow beak (B, which matches the sides views) is clearly unlike the three Half-Life items beside it. It is plausible as a crude Valve creature at a glance, but it is pale, flat-shaded and clean where the others are dark, grimy and organic, so a player would not take it for one of the game's.

M7.reason: Upright in every side view, standing on its four legs. The beak and the yellow cone sit at the front, underneath (BELOW, FRONT-LEFT), which gives a clear front.

M8.reason: SMAK's check returned no errors. 288 triangles is under the Half-Life median of 308 and well under the limit of 616 (twice the median, which is more than three quarters' 340). No open, inside-out or floating parts are visible in the sides or lineup views.
